title: "quarto-index placement probe"
# A table of contents on purpose: Quarto copies a heading's contents into the
# sidebar, so a mark in a heading is the case where an id minted inside the
# heading would appear twice in the page. It also puts the generated index
# section into a TOC, which the extension claims and this fixture checks.
toc: true
from: markdown-smart
filters:
  - index
---

# Marks the renderer moves

A locator must point at its mark wherever the rendered page ends up putting
it, and the locators of one entry must be numbered in the order the marks are
written — not in the order they happen to land on the page. The same term is
marked three times below: in a section heading, inside a table cell, and
inside a footnote, whose text a reader finds at the foot of the page rather
than where the reference sits.

## A [widget]{.index} in a heading

Body text under that heading.

| Part | Note |
|---|---|
| A [widget]{.index} in a table cell | the second column |

A footnote carries the third one.[^one]

[^one]: A [widget]{.index} in a footnote.

A mark that already carries an id of the author's own keeps it, and the index
links to that id instead of minting one: [gadget]{#my-gadget .index}.
